issue.title: [inbox-pipeline 06/07] Confirm, reject, and revise proposals safely (#105)

body:
Relay BB run pushed an update.

Pull request: #287

Tokens: 0 · Cost: $0.0000

Pushed successfully to branch `bb/relay-105-inbox-pipeline-06-07-confirm-reject-an-thr_c2g93czrgc`.

## Summary

Implements issue #105: confirm, reject, and revise for Processing proposals.

- **`inbox/proposalActions.ts`** (new): `confirmProposalWithClient`, `rejectProposalWithClient`, `reviseProposalWithClient`.
  - Confirm is the sole cross-destination write path: `database` envelopes go through the existing `createItemWithClient` choke point; `pageContent` envelopes go through a new `putBlockWithClient`. Persists `resultItemId`/`resultLabel` and locks `confirmed`. Idempotent under retry.
  - Reject locks `rejected` with no destination write; idempotent; refuses an already-confirmed proposal.
  - Revise replaces the complete envelope (including `entityKind`, so it can switch atomically between `database` and `pageContent`), appends a user-authored history entry, and refuses a locked proposal.
- **`docs/docPersistence.ts` / `docs/docStore.ts`**: added client-scoped `mutateDocWithClient`/`putBlockWithClient` so a page-content block append commits in the same transaction as the proposal's `confirmed` lock.
- **`inbox/inboxTickAction.ts`**: exported `appendHistoryEntry` (now with a selectable author) and `assertValidProposalEnvelope` for reuse.
- **`manifest/permissionManifest.ts`**: added `writable` to `ManifestDatabase` and scoped Semprec's own project grant so Inbox/Inbox item types are read-only and only Processing proposals is writable (grant separation).
- New tests in `proposalActions.test.ts` and a grant-separation test in `manifest.test.ts`.

Full workspace build and test suite (307 tests) pass.

Pushed to the existing branch `bb/relay-105-inbox-pipeline-06-07-confirm-reject-an-thr_c2g93czrgc` (updates PR #287), fast-forward `ff29e22..596e51b`.

## Summary

Addressed the two blocking findings from the code-review CI run on PR #287:

- **High (notification-before-commit):** `appendDocUpdateWithClient` was firing the realtime `notifyDocUpdate` hook immediately after inserting the `doc_updates` row, while the surrounding transaction (e.g. `confirmProposalWithClient`, which also updates the proposal's status) was still open — a later rollback could leave subscribers having observed a write that never persisted. Added a generic `runAfterCommit(client, callback)` primitive to `db/pool.ts`'s `withTransaction` and deferred the notification through it.
- **Medium (missing input validation):** `assertValidProposalEnvelope`'s `database` branch only checked that the target existed, not whether it was one of Semprec's own read-only-to-the-agent databases (Inbox, Inbox item types) — so a user-supplied `revise` could retarget a proposal there and bypass the manifest's `writable: false`. Extracted the shared module-id list to `seed/inboxPipelineKeys.ts`'s `SEMPREC_READ_ONLY_MODULE_IDS` (now reused by both the manifest and this validation) and reject such targets.

Added regression tests for both. Full build and test suite verified green (310/310 tests) before pushing.

## Summary

Addressed the two remaining medium-severity code-review findings on PR #287:

- **Correctness (`db/pool.ts`):** a synchronously-throwing `runAfterCommit` callback would propagate out of `withTransaction` after `COMMIT` had already succeeded — misreporting a committed transaction as failed to the caller, and silently skipping every callback queued after the one that threw. Each callback is now run in its own `try/catch`, so all of them execute once the transaction has committed, regardless of an earlier one failing.
- **Test coverage (`proposalActions.test.ts`):** added a test exercising `reviseProposalWithClient` from a `needsClarification` proposal (only `confirmed`/`rejected` are locked), verifying it transitions to `proposed` with the newly supplied envelope.

Full workspace build and test suite verified green (311/311 tests) before pushing.

## Summary

Addressed the newly reported medium-severity finding on PR #287:

- **Correctness:** `confirmProposalWithClient`'s `pageContent` branch cast `envelope.properties` to `{ flavour: string; fields?: Record<string, unknown>; children?: string[] }` without a runtime guarantee that `fields`/`children` actually had those shapes. Extended `assertValidProposalEnvelope` to require `fields` (if present) be a plain object and `children` (if present) be an array of strings, so the cast at confirm time is now backed by validation enforced on every `pageContent` envelope. Added regression tests for both malformed shapes.

Full workspace build and test suite verified green (313/313 tests) before pushing.
